questions.question: Kathasaritsagara, a literary work, was originally composed in which of the following languages?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sanskrit**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kathasaritsagara** is a famous literary work originally composed in **Sanskrit**.
 
• It is a renowned collection of Indian legends, fairy tales, and folk tales.
 
• The work is attributed to the author **Somadeva**, who compiled it in the 11th century.
 
• The title "Kathasaritsagara" translates to "Ocean of the Streams of Stories."
 
• This extensive work is an important source for understanding ancient Indian culture and literature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sanskrit** is an ancient Indian language and one of the oldest languages in the world.
 
• It is the liturgical language of Hinduism, Buddhism, and Jainism.
 
• Many classical Indian texts, including the Vedas, Upanishads, and epics like Mahabharata and Ramayana, were composed in Sanskrit.
 
• Sanskrit literature includes a rich tradition of poetry, drama, scientific, and philosophical texts.
 
• The language has significantly influenced many modern languages in India and around the world.

questions.question: Who is the author of the novel ‘The Moor’s Last Sigh’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Salman Rushdie**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Salman Rushdie** is the author of the novel** ‘The Moor’s Last Sigh’.**
 
• Sir Ahmed Salman Rushdie is a renowned Indian-born British-American novelist known for his distinctive blend of magic realism and historical fiction.
 
• His works often explore the connections, disruptions, and migrations between Eastern and Western civilizations, with a particular focus on the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Rushdie gained widespread acclaim with his second novel, "Midnight's Children" (1981), which not only won the Booker Prize but was also twice recognized as "the best novel of all winners" on the 25th and 40th anniversaries of the prize.
 
• In recognition of his literary achievements, Rushdie was elected a fellow of the Royal Society of Literature in 1983 and was honored with the title of Commandeur de l'Ordre des Arts et des Lettres by France in 1999.
 
• He was knighted in 2007 for his contributions to literature.
 
• Acknowledging his significant influence on contemporary literature, The Times ranked Rushdie 13th on its list of the 50 greatest British writers since 1945 in 2008. Since 2000, Rushdie has resided in the United States, where he continues to captivate audiences with his imaginative storytelling and thought-provoking narratives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Sir Vidiadhar Surajprasad Naipaul** was a Trinidadian-born British writer acclaimed for his fiction and nonfiction works in English.
 
• **John Stanley Melville Keay, **on the other hand, is a British historian, journalist, radio presenter, and lecturer known for his popular histories of India, the Far East, and China, particularly focusing on their colonization and exploration by Europeans.
 
• **Kiran Doshi,** a retired diplomat and educationist, has made a mark in literature as well. His novel "Jinnah Often Came to Our House" received The Hindu Prize in 2016, while his short story 'Miss Coelho, English Teacher' was shortlisted for the 2019 Commonwealth Prize.

questions.question: ‘The Race of my Life’ is the autobiography of which of the following sportsmen?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Milkha Singh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"The Race of My Life: An Autobiography" **is the **memoir of Indian athlete Milkha Singh**, which he co-authored with his daughter **Sonia Sanwalka**.
 
• The book served as the inspiration for the film **"Bhaag Milkha Bhaag."**
 
• Milkha Singh, also known as "The Flying Sikh," was born on November 20, 1929, and passed away on June 18, 2021.
 
• He was an accomplished track and field sprinter who discovered his talent for the sport while serving in the Indian Army. Singh holds the distinction of being the sole athlete to secure gold medals in the 400 meters event at both the Asian Games and the Commonwealth Games.
 
• Additionally, he claimed gold medals in the 1958 and 1962 Asian Games. Singh represented India in the 1956 Summer Olympics in Melbourne, the 1960 Summer Olympics in Rome, and the 1964 Summer Olympics in Tokyo. In recognition of his remarkable sporting achievements, he was honored with the Padma Shri, India's fourth-highest civilian award.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Pilavullakandi Thekkeparambil Usha**, a retired Indian track and field athlete, hails from Koothali near Perambra in the Kozhikode district of Kerala. She spent her formative years in Payyoli and has been closely associated with Indian athletics since 1979.
 
• **Mangte Chungneijang Mary Kom, **an Indian Olympic boxer, has also ventured into politics and served as a former Member of Parliament in the Rajya Sabha.
 
• Sourav Chandidas Ganguly, fondly known as Dada, is an Indian cricket commentator and former cricketer. Revered as the Maharaja of Indian Cricket, he has left an indelible mark on the sport.

questions.question: Which of the following books is an autobiography of the former American president Bill Clinton?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**My Life.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **My Life:-**

 
 
• **Bill Clinton's autobiography, "My Life," is a comprehensive and insightful account of his life and career.**
 
• The book covers everything from his childhood in Arkansas to his presidency and beyond.
 
• Clinton is a gifted storyteller, and he recounts his experiences with wit, candor, and humor. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Becoming:-**

 
 
• **Michelle Obama's memoir, "Becoming," is a deeply personal and inspiring account of her life, from her childhood in Chicago to her time as the First Lady of the United States.**
 
• With honesty and humor, she shares her experiences growing up in a strong and supportive family, her journey to Princeton University and Harvard Law School, her successful career as a lawyer, and her life-altering decision to enter public service.
 
 
 
• **Long Walk to Freedom: **
 
 
• **The Autobiography of Nelson Mandela is a powerful and inspiring account of the life of South Africa's first black president, Nelson Mandela.**
 
• Mandela, who spent 27 years in prison for his fight against apartheid, tells the story of his life with honesty, humility, and humor.
 
• The book is a testament to the power of the human spirit and the importance of fighting for justice and equality.
 
 
 
• **My Country My Life:-**
 
 
• **It is an autobiographical book written by Lal Krishna Advani.**
 
• The book was released on 19 March 2008 by Abdul Kalam, the eleventh President of India.

questions.question: In which of the following languages is ‘Childhood Days - A Memoir’ by Satyajit Ray written?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bengali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The ‘Childhood Days - A Memoir’** was written in **Bengali **by **Satyajit Ray**.
 
• **"Childhood Days - A Memoir" **is one of Ray's literary works where he delves into his own **childhood experiences**.
 
• In this memoir, Ray offers readers a glimpse into his formative years, growing up in Calcutta (now Kolkata), West Bengal, India.
 
• Through vivid storytelling and introspection, he captures the essence of his childhood, including his family life, education, friendships, and the cultural milieu of early 20th-century Bengal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Satyajit Ray** is widely recognized as one of the most influential film directors in cinema history. His acclaimed works, including **"The Apu Trilogy," "The Music Room," "The Big City," "Charulata," and the "Goopy-Bagha" trilogy, **highlight his remarkable talent for storytelling and his ability to capture the complexities of human experience on film.
 
• Born in Calcutta to author Sukumar Ray, Ray initially pursued a career as a commercial artist. However, his encounter with French filmmaker Jean Renoir and exposure to groundbreaking films like Vittorio De Sica's **"Bicycle Thieves" **inspired him to delve into independent filmmaking.
 
• In 1992, the Government of India honored Ray with the Bharat Ratna, its highest civilian award, in recognition of his outstanding contributions to the arts.
 
• Additionally, to commemorate Ray's birth centenary, the International Film Festival of India renamed its annual **Lifetime Achievement Award **to the **"Satyajit Ray Lifetime Achievement Award"** in 2021, acknowledging his enduring legacy in the world of cinema.
